claims.text: Loads on a bridge include live loads such as traffic and the dead load of the structure's own weight.

evidence.excerpt: live load - a temporary dynamic load such as vehicular traffic that is applied to a structure
dead load - a static load due to the weight of the structure itself

claims.assumptions: Generic definition of load types; no magnitudes.
claims.intended_visual: LOAD_ARROW on the deck labelled 'Load' (qualitative, not to scale)
claims.scope: conceptual; illustrative models; no member forces, capacities, stresses, safety factors or quantitative comparisons

claims.text: The deck directly supports traffic and is itself supported by the superstructure.

claims.intended_visual: COMPONENT_LABEL 'Deck'
claims.scope: conceptual; illustrative models; no member forces, capacities, stresses, safety factors or quantitative comparisons

claims.text: The superstructure is the part of a bridge that provides the horizontal span; it typically includes beams, girders, trusses and the deck.

evidence.excerpt: Structural parts of the bridge that provide the horizontal span.
It typically includes beams, girders, trusses, and the bridge deck.

claims.assumptions: Definition; the cap beams of a timber bent belong to the substructure (pier cap).
claims.intended_visual: HIGHLIGHT + COMPONENT_LABEL 'Superstructure'
claims.scope: conceptual; illustrative models; no member forces, capacities, stresses, safety factors or quantitative comparisons

claims.text: The substructure - abutments at the ends and piers in between - supports the superstructure, and abutments transfer loads from the superstructure to the foundation.

evidence.excerpt: substructure - the abutments and piers built to support the span of a bridge superstructure
abutment - part of bridge substructure at either end of bridge which transfers loads from superstructure to foundation
pier - a substructure unit that supports the spans of a multi-span superstructure at an intermediate location between its abutments

claims.assumptions: Definitions; in the timber model the trestle bents play the role of piers and the banks of the site the role of abutments (illustrative).
claims.intended_visual: CONCEPTUAL_LOAD_PATH from deck through supports to the ground
claims.scope: conceptual; illustrative models; no member forces, capacities, stresses, safety factors or quantitative comparisons

claims.text: A beam spans from one support to another and supports vertical loads.

evidence.excerpt: beam - a linear structural member designed to span from one support to another and support vertical loads

claims.intended_visual: HIGHLIGHT stringers (ghosted planks) + COMPONENT_LABEL 'Beams'
claims.scope: conceptual; illustrative models; no member forces, capacities, stresses, safety factors or quantitative comparisons

claims.text: A beam carries load through its resistance to bending.

evidence.excerpt: As a beam has strength from its bending resistance
girder - a horizontal flexural member that is the main or primary support for a structure

claims.assumptions: Qualitative; no stresses, deflections or capacities. The procedural model has not been analysed.
claims.intended_visual: CALLOUT 'Beams resist bending' on a stringer
claims.scope: conceptual; illustrative models; no member forces, capacities, stresses, safety factors or quantitative comparisons

claims.text: A cap at the top of a bent distributes the loads onto its columns, and columns are vertical members resisting compression.

bent - a substructure unit made up of two or more column or column-like members connected at their top-most ends by a cap
column - a general term applying to a vertical member resisting compressive stresses

claims.assumptions: Definitions; the posts of the illustrative trestle bents are treated as columns.
claims.intended_visual: CONCEPTUAL_LOAD_PATH stringer -> cap beam -> posts -> ground; REACTION_ARROW at the ground
